If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=-2x,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14261478/assets/ff94fdaad94c49b2cea35ab6ca8a59d7c99bfc58214bc211ed13a792c90a94eb.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le -2x\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{-2x}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{-2x}f(x,y)\,dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
